summary: Clearwater County pole platform with cabin, built 1934 and destroyed 1958; FFLA lists it as gone; no source describes what remains today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole platform with cabin at north end of ridge
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1958 per firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Forest Lookouts county list; FFLA lists it as Tower Gone

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site drive-up; no source describes remains on the ridge

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county list gives c.1934 while firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts give 1934. The story uses 1934 and notes the c.1934 wording.

notes_for_editor: Brief status gone and the 1958 destruction are confirmed by four sources. Thompson Point does not appear in the 2016 Clearwater National Forest lookout list (fs.usda.gov/media/259184), which was searched. Idaho Fire Lookouts gives no staffing history, so staffing is omitted. No source says whether the site is open to the public, so facts.access is omitted. No source gives the cause of the 1958 destruction. The 'Clearwater Timber Protective Association' agency comes from the county list only; firelookout.com uses the abbreviation CTPA.
